questions.stem: A can do a piece of work in 10 days and B in 15 days. Working together, how long will they take?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A can do a job in 12 days. He works alone for 3 days, then B joins him. They finish the remaining work together in 3 more days. In how many days can B alone do the full job?
questions.explanation:
Work done by A in 3 days = 3/12 = 1/4
Remaining = 3/4
A+B together finish 3/4 in 3 days → A+B per day = 1/4
A per day = 1/12
B per day = 1/4 − 1/12 = 3/12 − 1/12 = 2/12 = 1/6
B alone = 6 days
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A and B together complete a task in 8 days. B alone takes 12 days. In how many days can A alone do it?
questions.explanation:
A+B per day = 1/8
B per day = 1/12
A per day = 1/8 − 1/12 = 3/24 − 2/24 = 1/24
A alone = 24 days
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: 20 men can build a wall in 15 days. How many men are needed to finish it in 12 days?
questions.explanation:
Total man-days = 20 × 15 = 300
Men needed = 300 / 12 = 25

**Short Trick:** M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂ → 20 × 15 = M₂ × 12 → M₂ = 25.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A does 1/3 of a job in 5 days. At the same rate, how many days will he need to complete the entire job?
questions.explanation:
1/3 of work requires 5 days
Full work = 5 × 3 = 15 days
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A is twice as fast as B. B alone can complete a job in 18 days. How many days will A and B together take?
questions.explanation:
A is twice as fast → A takes half the time → A alone = 9 days
Together = 1/9 + 1/18 = 2/18 + 1/18 = 3/18 = 1/6
Time = 6 days
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A and B can do a work in 9 days, B and C in 12 days, A and C in 18 days. How long will all three together take?
questions.explanation:
Add all three equations:
2(A+B+C) = 1/9 + 1/12 + 1/18
= 4/36 + 3/36 + 2/36 = 9/36 = 1/4
A+B+C = 1/8
All three together = 8 days
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A can do a work in 20 days. After 5 days, A leaves and B alone finishes the rest in 12 days. How long would B take to do the complete work alone?
questions.explanation:
A's work in 5 days = 5/20 = 1/4
Remaining = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4
B finishes 3/4 of the work in 12 days
B for full work = 12 ÷ (3/4) = 12 × 4/3 = 16 days
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: 15 men working 8 hours/day can complete a project in 16 days. How many days will 12 men working 10 hours/day take?
questions.explanation:
Total man-hours = 15 × 8 × 16 = 1,920
Required days = 1,920 / (12 × 10) = 1,920 / 120 = 16 days

**Short Trick:** M₁D₁H₁ = M₂D₂H₂ → 15×16×8 = 12×D₂×10 → D₂ = 16.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A and B can together finish a work in 30 days. They work together for 20 days, then B leaves. A finishes the remaining work in 20 more days. How many days does A alone take for the full work?
questions.explanation:
Work done in 20 days together = 20/30 = 2/3
Remaining = 1 − 2/3 = 1/3
A finishes 1/3 in 20 days → A's full work = 20 × 3 = 60 days
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A and B can do a work in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, A and C in 20 days. In how many days can A alone do the work?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A can finish a work in 10 days, B in 15 days, C in 30 days. A and B work together for 3 days. Then A leaves and C joins B. How many more days do B and C take? What is the total?
questions.explanation:
A+B per day = 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6
Work in 3 days = 3/6 = 1/2
Remaining = 1/2
B+C per day = 1/15 + 1/30 = 2/30 + 1/30 = 3/30 = 1/10
Time for remaining 1/2 = (1/2) ÷ (1/10) = 5 more days
Total = 3 + 5 = 8 days
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A can do work in 6 days, B in 12 days, C in 4 days. A and B work together for 2 days, then C joins all of them. In how many total days is the work finished?
questions.explanation:
A+B per day = 1/6 + 1/12 = 2/12 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4
Work in 2 days = 2 × 1/4 = 1/2
Remaining = 1/2
All three per day = 1/6 + 1/12 + 1/4 = 2/12 + 1/12 + 3/12 = 6/12 = 1/2
Time for remaining 1/2 = 1 day
Total = 2 + 1 = 3 days
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A types 40 pages/hour and B types 20 pages/hour. They work together on a 360-page document for 5 hours, then B stops. How many more hours does A need to finish alone?
questions.explanation:
Pages done together in 5 hours = 5 × (40+20) = 5 × 60 = 300
Remaining = 360 − 300 = 60 pages
A's rate = 40 pages/hour
Time = 60 / 40 = 1.5 hours
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: 5 men can do a work in 12 days and 10 women can do the same in 8 days. In how many days will 4 men and 8 women together finish the work?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A, B, C together complete a work in 12 days. A alone takes 36 days. In how many days can B and C together complete the work?
questions.explanation:
A+B+C per day = 1/12
A per day = 1/36
B+C per day = 1/12 − 1/36 = 3/36 − 1/36 = 2/36 = 1/18
B and C together = 18 days
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A completes 40% of a job in 8 days. He then calls B and together they complete the remaining 60% in 4 days. How many days would B alone need for the full job?
questions.explanation:
A's rate = 40% / 8 days = 5% per day → A alone = 20 days
A+B combined rate = 60% / 4 days = 15% per day
B's rate = 15% − 5% = 10% per day
B alone = 100% / 10% = 10 days
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A is 50% more efficient than B. Together they complete a work in 12 days. How many days will A alone take?
questions.explanation:
A is 50% more efficient than B → A:B efficiency = 3:2
Let A's rate = 3k/day, B's rate = 2k/day
A+B = 5k = 1/12 → k = 1/60
A alone = 1/3k = 1/(3 × 1/60) = 60/3 = 20 days

**Short Trick:** If A:B = 3:2, A does 3/5 of work. A alone = total time × 5/3 = 12 × 5/3 = 20 days.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A and B together can finish a work in 15 days. They start together, but after 5 days A leaves. B completes the remaining work in 20 more days. How many days would A alone take?
questions.explanation:
Work done in 5 days together = 5/15 = 1/3
Remaining = 2/3
B alone finishes 2/3 in 20 days → B's rate = (2/3)/20 = 1/30
A's rate = 1/15 − 1/30 = 2/30 − 1/30 = 1/30
A alone = 30 days
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A is twice as efficient as B. Together they complete a piece of work in 14 days. In how many days can A alone finish the work?
questions.explanation:
Let A alone take x days → B alone takes 2x days (A is twice as efficient)
1/x + 1/2x = 1/14
2/2x + 1/2x = 3/2x = 1/14
2x = 42 → x = 21
A alone = 21 days
Verify: 1/21 + 1/42 = 2/42 + 1/42 = 3/42 = 1/14 ✓
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A can do a work in 18 days and B in 24 days. They work together for 6 days, after which A leaves. In how many more days will B alone finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
A per day = 1/18; B per day = 1/24
A+B per day = 1/18 + 1/24 = 4/72 + 3/72 = 7/72
Work done in 6 days = 6 × 7/72 = 42/72 = 7/12
Remaining = 1 − 7/12 = 5/12
B alone finishes 5/12 at rate 1/24 per day:
Days = (5/12) ÷ (1/24) = (5/12) × 24 = 10 days
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A alone finishes work in 30 days, B in 20 days. They work together for 6 days, then C joins and all three finish in 4 more days. How many days would C alone take?
questions.explanation:
A+B per day = 1/30 + 1/20 = 2/60 + 3/60 = 5/60 = 1/12
Work in 6 days = 6 × 1/12 = 1/2
Remaining = 1/2
A+B+C finish 1/2 in 4 days → A+B+C per day = (1/2)/4 = 1/8
C per day = 1/8 − 1/12 = 3/24 − 2/24 = 1/24
C alone = 24 days
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A, B, C work on alternate days starting with A (A on day 1, B on day 2, C on day 3, and so on). A, B, C can complete the work alone in 6, 8, and 12 days respectively. In how many days is the work done?
questions.explanation:
Work per 3-day cycle:
A does 1/6 + B does 1/8 + C does 1/12
= 4/24 + 3/24 + 2/24 = 9/24 = 3/8
After 2 full cycles (6 days): 2 × 3/8 = 3/4 done
Remaining = 1/4
Day 7 (A's turn): A does 1/6. Running total = 3/4 + 1/6 = 9/12 + 2/12 = 11/12
Remaining = 1/12
Day 8 (B's turn): B does 1/8 per day. To finish 1/12:
Time = (1/12) ÷ (1/8) = 8/12 = 2/3 of a day
Total = 7 + 2/3 = 7⅔ days
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A and B can do a work in 12 days. B and C can do it in 15 days. A, B, and C together do it in 10 days. In how many days can A and C together do the work?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
